problems.problem: Speaker misattribution in a 'verbatim' field. The opening-ritual entry gives Kirk's verbatim as "Wow, I'm Emily. Nice to meet you, Emily. Thank you." "Wow, I'm Emily" is the student's line; the researcher has fused two speakers' turns into a single quoted Kirk utterance and presented it at 'high' confidence. This is the exact failure mode the task warns about — putting words in a real person's mouth.
problems.evidence: Internal to the dossier: the string is self-evidently a student self-identifying. Cited source is YouTube WV29R1M25n8 (ID confirmed correct: 'Charlie Kirk Jubilee Surrounded' search returned https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WV29R1M25n8), but YouTube is unfetchable from this environment and captionfy.com/video/youtube/WV29R1M25n8 reports 'No subtitles in this video yet' — so the merged quote cannot be checked against the tape either.

problems.problem: Four positions rest on a single source URL that returns a hard 404. swellai.com/transcripts/charlie-kirk-podcast-transcript/trans-vs-detrans-charlie-s-prove-me-wrong-table-at-san-diego-state is dead. It is the sole citation for: the Scandinavia micro-concession ('I'll grant you that they have higher taxation and much more generous social benefits'), 'I stand corrected then...', 'I want to thank you for coming up. I want to pray for you,' and 'Buckle up, everybody.' The Scandinavia quote is additionally thematically implausible for an episode titled 'Trans vs. Detrans' and I could find no independent trace of it anywhere.
problems.evidence: curl -w HTTP:%{http_code} → HTTP:404, body renders '404: This page could not be found'. WebFetch → 'HTTP 404 Not Found'. Targeted web search for the exact string "I'll grant you that they have higher taxation and much more generous social benefits" returned zero matches across three query reformulations. Only 'Buckle up, everybody' is independently corroborated (confirmed as his standard podcast intro). The omny.fm episode page for that title exists, but its transcript is not retrievable and the episode is about detransition with Chloe Cole.

problems.problem: The gish-gallop 'Scandinavia' exemplar in rhetorical_moves is entirely uncorroborated. Economic freedom indices, Norway's sovereign wealth fund, NATO subsidy, 'tall poppy syndrome', billionaire counts, and the closing line 'you cannot have liberty without inequality' are presented as a single documented two-minute run at San Diego State, sourced to the same dead URL.
problems.evidence: Search for "you cannot have liberty without inequality" tied to Kirk returned nothing; the only near hit was an unrelated book, 'Libertarianism Without Inequality' by Michael Otsuka. No independent source for the run was found.

problems.problem: Bogus citation for a real quote. 'I rent it out. I'm there for 3 hours' is cited to www.cyclingeu.com/762551/charlie-kirk-qa-debate-cambridge-union/ at 'high' confidence. That domain does not resolve over TLS and is not a politics publication; searching it returns nothing. The quote itself is genuine.
problems.evidence: curl → 'LibreSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to www.cyclingeu.com:443', HTTP:000. WebFetch → 'Socket is closed' on two attempts. Web search for the domain returned no results from it. The real, verifiable text is at podscripts.co/podcasts/the-charlie-kirk-show/charlie-vs-the-university-of-cambridge: 'I do a campus event like a Texas A&M University. I rent it out. I'm there for three hours.' (note: 'three', not '3').

problems.problem: Wrong event date, twice, on a datable impossibility. Both San Francisco State entries ('Well, you seem pleasant. Are you married?' and 'Next question. Thank you very much.') are dated 2025-03-01. The Kirk/Riley Gaines SFSU event was 6 May 2025. The dossier's own content makes March impossible: the exchange turns on the Kilmar Abrego Garcia tattoo photo, a story that only broke in mid-April 2025.
problems.evidence: Search: 'Charlie Kirk and Riley Gaines visited San Francisco State University on May 6, 2025 at noon at the Mashouf Wellness Center field' (Golden Gate Xpress, KRON4, ABC7, Daily Caller 2025/05/07). Kirk's own X post announcing the event is dated to that week. The archived transcript's JSON-LD uploadDate is 2025-08-21 — an archive re-upload date, not the event date, which is likely what the researcher misread.

problems.problem: The '13% / 58%' stats-burst verbatim is sourced only to a partisan blog's admittedly cleaned, excerpted, partially-omitted transcript, yet it is the dossier's flagship exemplar for the single most persona-defining behaviour (the stats burst). The sentence's construction ('That's not systemic; that's cultural') reads as written cleanup, not speech, and independent reporting renders the same claim in materially different words.
problems.evidence: WebFetch of wltreport.com/2024/09/10/... confirms the string is present but reports: 'This is a commentary post, not a full transcript... The transcript is excerpted and incomplete', with an explicit bracketed omission marker '[The debate continues on topics of systemic racism... culminating in a heated exchange...]'. An independent secondary account renders Kirk's claim as 'Blacks represent 13% of the nation, and 58% of all murders' — different wording. The dossier's own gaps section concedes it could not trace the figure to any instance of him sourcing it.

problems.problem: A quote is attributed to a transcript it does not appear in. rhetorical_moves offers "Let me ask you, in the conflict of Israel versus Hamas, who's the good guy?" as a Cambridge Union example of the question-flip.
problems.evidence: Verbatim search of the cited podscripts Cambridge transcript: 'Israel versus Hamas, who's the good guy' — NOT PRESENT. (Four other Cambridge strings I checked in the same transcript were all PRESENT and exact.)

problems.problem: Directional slant on the Cambridge/Gaza exchange, stated as settled fact. The dossier calls the 'firestorm' line Kirk's 'one reliable tell' of having lost, and says the student's retort 'won the room'. The scoring of that exchange is contested, and the dossier cites only the one outlet whose framing it adopted.
problems.evidence: The quote is real ('It was also a moral truth that the war started because 1,300 Jews were killed and 200 were taken hostage. When you declare war on Israel, expect a firestorm in reaction!'). But contemporaneous accounts describe the student walking out while Kirk received applause and cheers, and the clip circulated overwhelmingly under titles like 'Charlie Kirk SILENCES Anti-Israel CAMBRIDGE Student' (YouTube E60FEt1YEE4), 'Charlie Kirk brilliantly defends Israel against clueless Cambridge University student' (qA39BlL06-A), and Mark Levin Show. Mediaite ('College Student Unloads on Charlie Kirk') is the outlier framing, and its URL returned HTTP 403 so its actual text could not be checked.

problems.problem: Confidence inflation on ASR-derived quotes. Multiple entries marked 'high' confidence are auto-generated YouTube captions republished by a fan archive, and the raw HTML shows visible speech-recognition corruption in the immediate vicinity of the quoted lines. Any 'verbatim' from charliekirk.co.za or singjupost is machine transcription, not a certified quote.
problems.evidence: Raw text pulled from charliekirk.co.za SFSU page contains 'Kilar Abrego Garcia' (Kilmar), 'Nian creed'/'Nyian creed' (Nicene), 'Phileman 116' (Philemon 1:16), 'Texas&M', and undelimited '>>' speaker turns with no speaker labels — meaning speaker attribution in these transcripts is inference, not data.

problems.problem: Possible conflation of two different Jubilee products. Eight quotes are attributed to WV29R1M25n8 (Sept 2024, 25 students), but a second Kirk 'Surrounded' release, 'Charlie Kirk vs 20 Liberal College Students', circulates with a 13 July 2025 date, and the 'college is a scam' thesis is indexed against it. None of the distinctive Jubilee quotes ('you're good at interrupting, not good at answering', 'do you pay to go to church', 'a little bit of a red herring and a little bit of a rabbit hole', 'back to the drawing board', 'I didn't go to college and I'm asking you very basic civic questions') could be located in any indexed transcript of the specific video cited.
problems.evidence: Two distinct listings exist: IMDb tt36255968 'Can 25 Liberal College Students Outsmart 1 Conservative? (feat. Charlie Kirk)' (2024) and Apple Podcasts id1000717042859 'Charlie Kirk vs 20 Liberal College Students' (2025). Search results give conflicting view counts (~3.5M vs 38M) and conflicting release dates for what is described as the same debate. The XX-chromosome definition and the circular-reasoning rebuttal are independently confirmed as Jubilee 'Surrounded' material, but not pinned to a specific episode.

problems.problem: The 'reasoning_pattern' fields are the researcher's imputed intent presented in the register of established fact, and the dossier concedes elsewhere that no source for his deliberate method exists.
problems.evidence: Examples: 'the queue and the clock become the alibi... never his willingness'; 'It buys ethos cheaply... makes the subsequent demolition read as civil rather than cruel'; 'the concession is the receipt for a swap that already happened'; 'by never ending on a period he never has to defend, only probe'. The dossier's own gap #8 states 'I could not find TPUSA's internal debate-training or talking-point materials... Everything here is reverse-engineered from output.' The observable behaviours are well-evidenced; the motives attached to them are not.

problems.problem: Material incompleteness that biases the persona FLATTERING rather than hostile. The delivery section describes near-uniform composure, courtesy and 'dry' humour, and the pressure-behaviour taxonomy has no category for his own personal cutting or for his hardest substantive positions. A partner built to this spec would be a soft strawman that fails the practice cases users most need.
problems.evidence: FactCheck.org (2025/09/viral-claims-about-charlie-kirks-words) confirms Kirk did in fact say the Civil Rights Act of 1964 was a 'huge mistake', made critical remarks about Martin Luther King Jr., made statements about Jewish donors, and made the 'some gun deaths... worth it' argument (5 Apr 2023, TPUSA Faith, Utah) — none of which appear as positions or as register in the dossier. The raw SFSU transcript also carries markedly personal jabs in the disputed exchange ('Was your mom married?', 'Does anyone love you in your life?') that the ASR does not attribute cleanly and that the 'refuse to match heat / deadpan' framing elides.

problems.problem: Quantitative delivery claims are asserted in the summary without the hedge that the gaps section supplies. A downstream builder reads the summary.
problems.evidence: Summary states turn lengths (15–45s / 30–90s / 2–8min), 'he rarely says um', and a specific accelerate-then-drop prosodic contour as description. Gaps #1 and #2 concede: 'No quantitative measurement of his speech rate exists in any source I could find' and 'No systematic data on turn lengths. My estimates... are reconstructed from transcripts and event reports, not measured.'

problems.problem: Unverified decorative detail attached to a verified fact. The Cambridge/scripture entry claims 'the Bible on his table was prominent enough that South Park's parody reproduced it'.
problems.evidence: South Park 'Got a Nut' (S27E2, premiered 6 Aug 2025, Cartman parodying Kirk, pulled from Comedy Central reruns after 10 Sept 2025) is fully verified. The specific Bible-on-the-table reproduction claim is not attested in any source found and appears to be the researcher's inference.

corrected_recommendation:
The dossier's central thesis — that Kirk ran one repeatable format machine, and that the format explains the style — survives and is unusually well-sourced in its core. Roughly two-thirds of the verbatims I could check came back exact. But it must not be shipped as-is; specific entries are misattributed or unsourceable.

DROP outright:
1. The opening-ritual verbatim "Wow, I'm Emily. Nice to meet you, Emily. Thank you." — it merges the student's words into Kirk's. The BEHAVIOUR (name exchange, name reuse) is well attested and should be kept; replace the verbatim with a description, or with a Kirk-only fragment sourced to a checkable transcript.
2. The rhetorical_moves line "Let me ask you, in the conflict of Israel versus Hamas, who's the good guy?" — not present in the cited transcript. The Cambridge question-flip move stands on the verified "Let me ask you a question without you interrupting me" pattern; delete this exemplar.
3. The Scandinavia gish-gallop exemplar in rhetorical_moves (freedom indices / sovereign wealth fund / NATO / tall poppy / "you cannot have liberty without inequality"). No surviving source. Keep the gish-gallop move; substitute a verified example.

AMEND:
4. All four swellai.com-sourced entries: mark confidence LOW and status UNVERIFIED, or re-source before use. The dead URL currently props up "I'll grant you that…", "I stand corrected then…", "I want to pray for you", and "Buckle up, everybody". Only "Buckle up, everybody" is independently confirmed. The micro-concession and the pastoral-close behaviours are plausible and worth modelling, but not as quotable verbatims.
5. Fix the cyclingeu.com citation → https://podscripts.co/podcasts/the-charlie-kirk-show/charlie-vs-the-university-of-cambridge, and correct the quote to "I do a campus event like a Texas A&M University. I rent it out. I'm there for three hours."
6. Fix both San Francisco State dates: 2025-03-01 → 2025-05-06.
7. Downgrade the 13%/58% verbatim from a quotable line to a paraphrased behaviour ("cites a Black-population-share vs murder-share ratio, unsourced, as a conversation terminator"). Do not let a voice persona speak the sentence "13% of the population commits 58% of the murders. That's not systemic; that's cultural." — it exists only in one partisan blog's self-described cleaned, excerpted transcript.
8. Neutralise the Cambridge/Gaza entry. State that the exchange is scored oppositely by opposing outlets — Mediaite frames it as the student landing, while the clip circulated far more widely as a Kirk win with the student leaving to applause — and drop "his one reliable tell" and "won the room" as findings.
9. Re-label every "reasoning_pattern" as observer inference, not Kirk's stated method. The behaviours are evidenced; the motives are reverse-engineered, as the dossier's own gap #8 admits.
10. Move the unmeasured cadence and turn-length numbers out of the summary into an explicitly-estimated section, or carry the hedge inline.
11. Delete the South Park Bible-on-the-table detail (the parody itself is verified; that detail is not).

ADD, to prevent misrepresentation by omission — this is the most consequential fix:
12. The dossier's Kirk is too civil. It has no register for the FactCheck.org-confirmed hard positions (Civil Rights Act a "huge mistake", MLK remarks, the "worth it" gun-deaths framing) and no pressure behaviour for his own personal jabs. A practice partner built only on "flat, gracious, near-monotone reasonableness" is a flattering strawman, which fails the brief in the opposite direction from the usual error and will not prepare anyone for the exchanges they actually want to rehearse.

Finally: the gaps section is the strongest part of the document and is materially accurate — I independently confirmed the FactCheck.org findings (Politicon/Cenk, 16M+ views, Stephen King's apology, the 5 Apr 2023 TPUSA Faith Utah gun-deaths quote), the Ben Gleib dolphin-fetus incident (Oct 2021, on Kirk's own show), the Middlehurst and Troutt sourcing caveats, and the assassination facts. Those caveats should be promoted into the persona spec itself rather than left as footnotes, because a builder who reads only summary + positions will ship the errors the gaps section already warns against.
surviving_claims: The 'Prove Me Wrong' format description is fully verified: canopy reading 'prove me wrong', Kirk seated under a tent, challengers at a mic, ~3-hour events, MAGA hats thrown to the crowd (The Independent Florida Alligator, 27 Feb 2025, all five checks exact).
The published queue rule is verified verbatim from TPUSA's own event promotion: 'Don't agree with Charlie? Great, you go to the front of the line.' (ABC News, 10 Sep 2025).
The 'by what standard' regress is verified verbatim in the Cambridge Union transcript: 'Okay, why? By what standard? By what book? By what scholar? By what author? By what worldview?'
The tu quoque with the sarcastic 'I'm sorry' marker is verified verbatim: 'I'm sorry, didn't you just mandate a vaccine for the last couple of years?' (Cambridge Union, 19 May 2025).
Enumeration plus 'so on and so forth' as list-terminator is verified: '...free markets, rule of law, individual initiative, entrepreneurship, the constitution, so on and so forth.'
Scripture-as-premise is verified: '...we take the biblical idea to train a child up in the ways in which they will go...' (Cambridge Union).
The out-of-knowledge handling is verified verbatim: 'I don't know enough about the case. Why is she on life support?' (Oxford Union, 20 May 2025).
The acoustics time-buying device is verified verbatim: 'I'm sorry, just to make sure I'm hearing the question and it's not your fault, it's the acoustics.' (Oxford Union).
The floor-holding-plus-redefinition tic is verified verbatim: 'Hold on a second. She's brain dead. But let's re-examine what being dead means.' (Oxford Union).

The anecdote-to-category move is verified verbatim and in full: 'One of the most powerful things I get to do is go to college campuses and all the time I meet young kids that were babies that were scheduled for abortions that were conceived in rape.' The two-ultrasound prop and 'Do we know which one is which?' are likewise verified in the same transcript.

The Lord of the Rings put-down is verified verbatim and the dossier's context is correct — he is dismissing the Netflix series Baby Reindeer: 'Which was a complete fiction, by the way... It's a mythology, no different than Lord of the Rings. There's no basis for this.'

The wording-not-substance self-correction is verified verbatim, with the dossier's context (an opponent who had read the underlying bill — the Inflation Reduction Act pill-penalty provision) correct: 'Yes, but I should have been much more precise... But I acknowledge I could have been more precise.'
The deadpan-under-abuse behaviour is verified verbatim, including the free-hat detail: 'Well, you seem pleasant. Are you married?' and, later in the same exchange, 'Do you want a hat?'

The courteous hard cut is verified, and — contrary to my initial suspicion — it does immediately follow the Abrego Garcia photo exchange, exactly as the dossier claims. Raw transcript: '>> Trump has used this labeling to try and prove that he's a part of >> Next question. Thank you very much.' Kirk also visibly declined to resolve the exhibit, first counter-questioning ('why did his girlfriend blur it out in all the images she posted?') and then cutting.

The campus opener is verified verbatim: 'It feels good to win, doesn't it? This is what free speech is all about.' (UF, 27 Feb 2025), as is the civics-quiz-plus-crowd-turn ('This is what you're paying for', after quizzing a UF history instructor on Churchill and the Dardanelles).

The 'waterfall' characterisation is verified verbatim in Chris Satullo's 16 Sep 2025 essay: 'He would respond with a waterfall of smooth rhetoric, peppered with assertions of fact that were often dubious, sometimes flat-out false. Man, the guy was good at political messaging, quick on his feet, never losing his cool...'
'Buckle up, everybody' is confirmed as his standard podcast opener, independent of the dead swellai URL.

The definition-demand move is substantively confirmed: Kirk defined a woman biologically by XX chromosomes on Jubilee 'Surrounded' and rejected 'someone who identifies as a woman' as circular, using a table analogy.

Every claim in the gaps section that I checked is accurate: the Politicon 2018 'slur' was Kirk shouting Cenk Uygur's name and the false post exceeded 16 million views in under two days; Stephen King did apologise and acknowledge Kirk was cherry-picking Leviticus in response to Ms. Rachel; the 'some gun deaths worth it' quote is accurate and correctly dated to 5 Apr 2023, TPUSA Faith, Utah; the dolphin-fetus incident was Ben Gleib on Kirk's own show in October 2021 with Kirk answering 'Without a doubt'; Naima Troutt's exchange is Sept 2024 Jubilee, covered by Interview Magazine and The Guardian and disputed by The College Fix over the 'creepy smile' remark; Tilly Middlehurst's happiness reductio is real and widely circulated.
The biographical frame is correct: Kirk was killed on 10 September 2025 at Utah Valley University while taking questions during a campus event.
South Park 'Got a Nut' (S27E2, premiered 6 Aug 2025) does parody Kirk via Cartman, and Comedy Central pulled it from reruns after the assassination.
Bentham's Bulldog, 'Charlie Kirk's Bad Arguments', exists and is dated March 2025 as cited.
